question: What defines a complete abortion in early pregnancy?

options.A: The cervix opens wide without any tissue passing out
options.B: All products of conception are totally expelled from the uterus
options.C: The fetus is expelled but the placenta remains inside
options.D: Bleeding stops temporarily but the pregnancy continues

explanation: A complete abortion means everything, including the fetus, membranes, and placenta, has left the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does bleeding typically stop or slow down significantly after a complete abortion?

options.A: Clotting factors instantly multiply across the entire body
options.B: Low blood pressure naturally forces the bleeding to dry up
options.C: Strong uterine contractions close off the open blood vessels
options.D: The patient drinks large amounts of cold water to cool down

explanation: When the uterus is completely empty, it contracts firmly, which squeezes the open blood vessels shut to stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the typical state of the external cervical os during a speculum examination for a complete abortion?
explanation: Once all pregnancy tissue has passed and the uterus contracts, the cervix closes back up. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic stating she passed a fleshy mass an hour ago, and her severe lower abdominal cramps have now stopped completely. What is the most likely initial assessment finding?

options.A: An open cervical os with active heavy bleeding
options.B: A rigid, severely tender abdomen with high fever
options.C: A greatly enlarged uterus with fetal parts felt
options.D: A closed cervix and a uterus smaller than expected

explanation: Passing the tissue means the abortion is likely complete, resulting in a closed cervix and a smaller, contracted uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which condition features persistent bleeding and cramping with an open cervical os, unlike a complete abortion?
explanation: An incomplete abortion still has tissue inside the uterus, so the cervix stays open and bleeding continues. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is NOT a common differential diagnosis for bleeding in early pregnancy?
explanation: Term labor happens at the end of a full pregnancy, not in early pregnancy when bleeding first occurs. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary ultrasound finding that confirms a complete abortion?

options.A: Multiple grape-like clusters filling the whole uterus
options.B: An empty uterine cavity with a thin endometrial lining
options.C: A gestational sac containing a live, active fetal heart
options.D: A thick mass of retained placental tissue and blood clots

explanation: An ultrasound showing an empty uterus with a thin lining proves that all products of conception have been expelled. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is a transvaginal ultrasound preferred over a general abdominal scan when checking for complete abortion?

options.A: It is completely painless and avoids touching the vaginal area
options.B: It gives a much clearer, closer view of the empty uterine cavity
options.C: It costs nothing for the patient to perform in rural clinics
options.D: It requires the patient to drink large amounts of water first

explanation: Transvaginal probes sit closer to the uterus, allowing midwives and doctors to clearly see if any tissue remains inside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient has a confirmed complete abortion on ultrasound with minimal spotting and stable vital signs. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.A: Perform a repeat manual vacuum aspiration to clean the lining
options.B: Rush the patient to the theater for immediate surgical evacuation
options.C: Provide supportive care, reassurance, and discharge instructions
options.D: Start high-dose intravenous antibiotics and admit for two weeks

explanation: Because the uterus is already empty, surgery is unnecessary, and the patient only needs support and recovery advice. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h5)

question: When are prophylactic antibiotics typically recommended for a patient with a complete abortion?

options.A: Only when the patient requests pain relief medications
options.B: Never under any circumstances in maternity care settings
options.C: Only if there are signs of infection such as fever or foul discharge
options.D: For every single patient regardless of their physical examination

explanation: Routine antibiotics are not needed for a clean, complete abortion unless infection is clinically suspected. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is immediate contraceptive counseling important following a complete abortion?

options.A: Fertility can return as early as two weeks after the event
options.B: Hormonal contraceptives instantly cure uterine infections
options.C: Women are legally required to wait two years before conceiving
options.D: Pregnancy is biologically impossible for a full year afterward

explanation: Ovulation can resume very quickly after a miscarriage, so patients need birth control guidance right away if they wish to avoid immediate pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is an important part of holistic post-abortion care besides physical healing?

options.A: Strict bed rest at home for at least one full month
options.B: Isolating the patient from family members to ensure rest
options.C: Providing compassionate emotional support and grief counseling
options.D: Mandatory referral to a psychiatric hospital for strong sedatives

explanation: Emotional support helps patients process the loss and ensures they receive holistic, empathetic care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h6)
